# Appendix D — Built-in tables

Both tables are read-only on the PCX2: they power up holding exactly what the 4.x drivers write and ignore writes (measured on a Matrox m3D, PCX2 rev 1, 2026-10-17). The same values are in `renderer/vid_powervr_pcx_tables.h`.

## Fog table (BAR0 dwords 0x080–0x0FF)

128 entries, FogTable[i] = floor(256 × 2^(−i/128)), entry 0 clamped to 255. Only bits 7:0 are used. The fog factor for a pixel is `FogTable[index & 0x7F] >> min(index >> 7, 9)`, with `index = depth >> FOGAMOUNT` (reference, "Fog").

Values by index (hex):

```
00: ff fe fd fb fa f9 f7 f6 f5 f3 f2 f1 ef ee ed ec
10: ea e9 e8 e6 e5 e4 e3 e2 e0 df de dd db da d9 d8
20: d7 d6 d4 d3 d2 d1 d0 cf ce cd cb ca c9 c8 c7 c6
30: c5 c4 c3 c2 c1 c0 bf be bd bc ba b9 b8 b7 b6 b6
40: b5 b4 b3 b2 b1 b0 af ae ad ac ab aa a9 a8 a7 a6
50: a5 a5 a4 a3 a2 a1 a0 9f 9e 9e 9d 9c 9b 9a 99 99
60: 98 97 96 95 94 94 93 92 91 90 90 8f 8e 8d 8d 8c
70: 8b 8a 8a 89 88 87 87 86 85 84 84 83 82 82 81 80
```

## Divider table (BAR0 dwords 0x200–0x3FF)

512 dwords: 256 pairs of (mask, coefficient), the driver's `ReciprocalTable`. PCX1 drivers load it into RAM on the chip; on the PCX2 it is ROM and no driver writes it. Reads on the PCX2 are order-dependent: a sweep upward from 0x200 returns every entry, but jumping ahead after reading 0x200 returns 0 until the sweep reaches that entry (reference, "Measured on the Matrox m3D"). How the PCX1 ISP uses the mask half is an open question.
